Where Coinglass is still better

Honesty over marketing: Coinglass covers more venues, keeps multi-year archives, and ships institutional dashboards (ETF flows breakdowns, exchange balance tracking, dozens of indicators) that MarginPad does not try to replicate. If your work needs years of archived derivatives history or those specific dashboards — and the subscription is worth it to you — Coinglass is a strong product.

MarginPad's bet is different: the tools a trader opens daily — where are liquidations, what is funding, where do clusters sit right now — should be free, fast and open, with no account between you and the data. That is the entire product philosophy, and it is also why the site includes a free paper trading terminal to act on what the data shows.

Frequently asked questions

Is there a free alternative to Coinglass?

Yes. MarginPad keeps a live liquidation heatmap, per-coin liquidation maps for 18 coins, a real-time liquidations feed from 10 exchanges, funding rates, open interest and long/short data free, with no login and no paid tier gating the core tools.

What does Coinglass gate behind Prime?

As of August 2026, Coinglass places its advanced liquidation heatmap models and real-time refresh behind the paid Prime plan, limits historical depth on the free tier, and prices API access from around $29 per month (about $299 per month for commercial use).

Is MarginPad's liquidation data real or estimated?

Both, clearly labelled: the liquidations feed and map bubbles are real events streamed from exchange websockets, while the heatmap cluster layer is a model estimate from open interest and leverage profiles — the same class of estimate every heatmap provider uses, labelled as such.

When is Coinglass the better choice?

If you need years of archived derivatives data, broader venue coverage or its institutional dashboards and are willing to pay for them. For the everyday liquidation toolkit, MarginPad keeps it free.
